"Universities, municipal corporations and companies are examples of artificial persons. A legal person can own property, enter contracts, sue and be sued in its own name. Indian courts have recognised Hindu idols as juristic persons capable of owning property."
(i) Which of these has been recognised as a juristic person by Indian courts? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'corporation sole' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: A company acts through its directors. (2)
items.answer: (i) A Hindu idol (ii) A corporation consisting of a single office-holder, such as the office of a Postmaster General, that continues beyond the individual. (iii) An artificial person has no physical existence and cannot act by itself.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) A Hindu idol (ii) A corporation consisting of a single office-holder, such as the office of a Postmaster General, that continues beyond the individual. (iii) An artificial person has no physical existence and cannot act by itself.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about companies and lifting the corporate veil is correct?
items.answer: Courts lift the corporate veil in cases of fraud, tax evasion, enemy character and avoidance of legal obligations.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: A private company needs at least two members; a public company needs seven. Their liability is limited to the unpaid amount on their shares. A company has perpetual succession.
options: Shareholders are personally liable for all company debts.
Courts lift the corporate veil in cases of fraud, tax evasion, enemy character and avoidance of legal obligations.
A company ends when its main shareholder dies.
A private company must have at least seven members.

items.stem:
Statement: A company continues even if all members change.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It has perpetual succession.
items.markingKey: (c) It has perpetual succession.
options: The separate personality of a company may be misused as a cloak for fraud.
They combine partnership flexibility with limited liability.
It has perpetual succession.
It is a separate legal entity distinct from its members.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about sole proprietorship, partnership and LLP:
I. Registration of a partnership firm is optional, but an unregistered firm cannot sue third parties to enforce contracts.
II. An LLP has perpetual succession and the liability of partners is limited to their agreed contribution.
III. In an LLP one partner is not responsible for the misconduct of another partner.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I and III only
All of them
II only
II and III only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about companies and lifting the corporate veil is NOT correct?
items.answer: A company ends when its main shareholder dies.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. A company has perpetual succession.
options: The Companies Act 2013 permits a company to be formed for any lawful purpose by registration.
Courts lift the corporate veil in cases of fraud, tax evasion, enemy character and avoidance of legal obligations.
A company ends when its main shareholder dies.
Shares of a public company are freely transferable, while a private company restricts transfer.

items.stem: What is meant by 'designated partner' in the context of sole proprietorship, partnership and LLP?
items.answer: A partner of an LLP responsible for compliance with the LLP Act.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: designated partner correctly explained as a partner of an LLP responsible for compliance with the LLP Act.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on sole proprietorship, partnership and LLP and answer the questions that follow.
"A sole proprietorship has no separate legal existence from its owner. In an LLP one partner is not responsible for the misconduct of another partner. Registration of a partnership firm is optional, but an unregistered firm cannot sue third parties to enforce contracts."
(i) The LLP Act was passed in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'sole proprietorship' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: A partner can bind the firm by acts done in the course of business. (2)
items.answer: (i) 2008 (ii) A business owned and controlled by one person who bears unlimited liability. (iii) Each partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners (mutual agency).
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 2008 (ii) A business owned and controlled by one person who bears unlimited liability. (iii) Each partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners (mutual agency).

items.stem:
Read the following statements about legal persons: natural and artificial:
I. Only human beings can be legal persons.
II. An artificial person continues to exist even when its members change.
III. Indian courts have recognised Hindu idols as juristic persons capable of owning property.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (c) I is incorrect: The law also recognises artificial persons such as companies and corporations. II is correct. III is correct.
options: All of them
I only
II and III only
III only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about legal persons: natural and artificial is NOT correct?
items.answer: An artificial person can act without any human agent.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. It acts through human agents such as directors.
options: An artificial person can act without any human agent.
An artificial person acts through human agents such as directors and officers.
An artificial person continues to exist even when its members change.
Universities, municipal corporations and companies are examples of artificial persons.
